correctness.rationale: In units of a, the Jacobian is a block diagonal operator −2P_j (P_j the radial rank-one orthogonal projector), plus common injection of K times the mean perturbation, K=[[x,−y],[y,x]]. Noncollinearity gives a rank-two phase-balance derivative and precisely M−2 tangential neutral directions. A rank-two determinant update gives characteristic polynomial [t(t+2)]^(M−2) det(t(t+2)I−[(t+1)I−S]K), where S=2 mean(P_j)−I has eigenvalues ±d. The trace in the determinant is 2x(t+1) and det([(t+1)I−S]K)=((t+1)^2−d²)(x²+y²). This reproduces all factors including exceptional t=0,−2 by polynomial identity. With the notation b_j of the proof, b_1 b_2−b_3=2(1−x)[y²+(2−x)(4−x)] and (b_1 b_2−b_3)b_3−b_1²b_4=4H. For x≥2 b_1 fails, and for 1≤x<2 the first determinant fails. For 0<x<1, b_1,b_4 and the first determinant are positive, so H>0 forces b_3>0 and then b_2>0, which completes strict Hurwitz equivalence. In u=y², H has positive leading coefficient, negative constant term and is strictly negative at u=x(2−x); its unique positive root decreases strictly with d². At equality the stated factorization gives a simple imaginary pair and a Hurwitz quadratic. At x=1/2, y=1 the exact threshold is d²=13/18, with an unstable square (H<0 and no imaginary or zero collective roots) and an attracting antipodal-pair polygon at φ=π/6 (d²=3/4), at the same coefficients. Independently replayed symbolic identities and 12 exact rational four-node Jacobian comparisons: python3 /workspace/replay/stuart_landau.py (SymPy). If Ω=0 the solution is an equilibrium, so the spectrum is interpreted as characteristic rates, not as multipliers of an orbit with an intrinsic period. For Ω≠0 the co-rotating transformation is periodic and the exponents give the claimed Floquet real parts. No nonlinear Hopf or single-orbit asymptotic-attraction claim is made.
